comment: The federated exchange model is anchored on shared standards and common identifiers from the core registries, while the guidance also supports intermittent-connectivity and store-and-forward operation. In such settings, identifier use should not depend on uninterrupted access to a central registry, and locally assigned identifiers must be reconcilable without creating collisions or ambiguous identity links.

reviewer.name: Timothy W. Cook; Luciana Cavalini, MD, PhD (co-author)

public.text: The federated exchange model is anchored on shared standards and common identifiers from the core registries, while the guidance also supports intermittent-connectivity and store-and-forward operation. In such settings, identifier use should not depend on uninterrupted access to a central registry, and locally assigned identifiers must be reconcilable without creating collisions or ambiguous identity links.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a requirement that identifier schemes used in federated or intermittently connected deployments support collision-resistant local assignment where needed, offline persistence of identifiers already issued, and deterministic reconciliation when connectivity is restored, without requiring uninterrupted access to a central registry.
